Check who keeps needing help

By v/hNovember 17, 2026Note

Originally shared
on LinkedIn

View the post ↗← All journal entries

An everyday utility can work most of the time and still fail the same person every day.

During development, we would record completed jobs and the help needed for each person's repeated uses. We would then check whether the same difficulty keeps returning for the same people.

Someone might learn to place every object at a precise angle to make a prototype work. Their later attempts could look more successful while the product still depends on that extra care.

A proposed comparison would ask those people to repeat the same task after a design change. Count the adjustments alongside the quality of the result, and compare the effort with their current routine.

For v/h, the local agent should help handle ordinary variation in its inputs. The housing and controls have to support that goal too. A better average is incomplete evidence if the same people still have to do the difficult part.

Our first utility is in development. The placement example is illustrative, and these are proposed checks, not findings from user trials.
